props.html: The three nights a retreat books

rows.text: The group has been traveling all day and the first night’s job is conversation. A duo plays it at a level people talk across, so colleagues who flew in from three offices can actually meet.
The night with the awards, the remarks and the number for the year. Music runs up to the moment and stops while the speaker is still steps from the microphone.
The loud one. A quartet gets people dancing inside whatever limit and curfew the resort sets, and where the retreat wants a named act in front, Tejas Singh leads the roster.

props.html: Several nights can go on one contract. Want some ideas? Eight evenings, with the size each one needs, are in corporate retreat evening ideas in Vail, and a dinner in town is covered on our client dinners page.

Mornings and firesides have their own acts. Firstwater is a seventy-five-minute sound bath with the whole group lying on the floor, placed to open a morning or close an evening, and René Moffatt plays his own folk and Americana songs on a deck or by a fire after dinner.

props.title: Offsites for remote and hybrid companies.
props.lede: The people organising company offsites now mostly work remote or hybrid themselves, 91 percent of them in the most recent industry report, and 57 percent of fully remote companies call the offsite essential to the business. Most gather once or twice a year for a few weekdays, and Colorado is where a lot of them do it, because it has a hub airport a distributed team can reach without connecting and a mountain evening within two hours of it.

props.html: A remote team’s offsite has a different first night from any other corporate booking. People who know each other’s faces from a video grid are in one place for the first time, and a duo through the arrival dinner gives colleagues who’ve never met a reason to stand in the same corner. The last night is the one where the whole company dances.

Company offsite ideas in Colorado for remote teams has where remote teams go and seven evenings built for them. The Americana band is the Colorado evening for a group that flew in for it, and live band karaoke is the night a remote team quotes back to itself on video calls for the rest of the year.

props.title: What a resort date adds to a quote.
props.lede: A resort date costs more than a Denver metro one, and it’s worth knowing why before you read a quote.

props.html: The first is the drive. Vail and Beaver Creek are a mountain highway from Denver, and Aspen is most of a working day each way. Travel is priced with the date, so what your leadership approves looks like a Denver evening with a drive attached.

The second is the night at the far end. A band that finishes late in Aspen stays the night, so a far-resort date carries a night’s lodging, billed at cost. The I-70 towns are close enough that most dates don’t.
The third is the calendar. A holiday weekend is priced above a standard date across Colorado, and whatever the calendar adds is in the price we send you.

items.q: What does the resort need to provide?
items.a: One or two dedicated 20-amp circuits within reach of the performance area, not shared with catering warmers or a lighting truss, which is the most common cause of a setup problem. Setup runs 45 to 90 minutes depending on size, strike 30 to 60, timed to the dock and elevator windows the venue gives us.

items.q: How loud is it, and do you honor sound caps and curfews?
items.a: The welcome dinner plays at the level of the conversation, and the last night plays like a dance band. Mountain venues run their own rules, so tell us the cap and the curfew when you book and both go into the plan, with the set built to land on the curfew.

items.q: Can the band play outdoors at altitude?
items.a: Yes, on a covered, level and dry performance area with power run to it and a move-indoors call time written before the day, because mountain evenings drop fast. The corridor runs from about 7,900 feet in Aspen to roughly 9,600 in Breckenridge, where singers and horns pace a night differently and the temperature swing means more retuning.

items.q: Do you play company offsites for remote and hybrid teams?
items.a: Yes, and the offsite is now the most common reason a company books a mountain evening. Tell us the dates, the venue and roughly how many are flying in, and we'll plan every evening of the stay on one contract.
